title: EU AI Act Article 11 Technical Documentation — What High-Risk Providers Must Produce and Maintain
context: 2026-08-29 engine cycle — Article 11 requires comprehensive technical documentation for Annex III high-risk systems, aligned with Annex IV specifications, binding from August 2, 2026
body: EU AI Act Article 11 mandates that providers of high-risk AI systems draw up and maintain technical documentation that demonstrates compliance with the requirements of Chapter 2 (Articles 8-15). Annex IV specifies the minimum contents: a general description of the system, its design and development methodology, performance metrics, risk management documentation, and instructions for use. For Annex III systems this obligation is binding from August 2, 2026. The Council of AI provides a verified measurement credential framework that slots into the Annex IV evidentiary structure — rather than self-attesting that a risk control works, the provider can supply a signed measurement from the Council measurement board showing the control was independently observed. Key requirements: (1) the technical documentation must be kept for 10 years after the system is placed on the market; (2) it must be in a language easily understood by the relevant national competent authority; (3) the provider must demonstrate that appropriate human oversight measures (Article 14) are documented and verified. The honest boundary is monitored containment: providers must show the system's risk surface is measured and watched, not that it is provably safe. Concretely, for each Annex IV element, pair a declaratory statement with a verified measurement credential from the Council measurement infrastructure, ensuring audit-readiness under Article 11.
references: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Annex IV — technical documentation for high-risk AI systems
